<!--
  layout-pattern — how a page arranges its regions: the regions and their landmarks, the hierarchy,
  the arrangement at each width class, and where each navigation system sits. The shell of an
  application is a layout pattern. Text-first and tool-neutral.
  Lives at: `design/layout-patterns/<pattern-slug>.md` — one page per pattern.
  Authorship: curated. SLO: 180d, AND stale whenever any page `realizes:` names is updated after this one —
    either trigger fires. The timer stays alongside the edge: a pattern can drift from what shipped even
    though the product base it realizes has not changed.
  Owner: fixed to `design`, do not substitute.
  Distinct from: a `ui-component` — one reusable part's anatomy, behavior and states — and a
    `design-system` interaction pattern — a composition of components solving a recurring interaction
    problem. A layout pattern arranges regions; it places components and navigation systems in them and
    does not specify them. A surface follows a layout pattern through its Layout patterns bullet, and an
    `information-architecture` page through `layout-patterns:`; a dialog or panel opened from the
    page's chrome names the region it opens from through its Opened from bullet.
  Discipline: the page rules are the ones a page-structure review holds a page to. Every region sits in a
    landmark; a page has one `banner`, one `main` and one `contentinfo`; a landmark role that repeats is
    labeled; hierarchy comes from order, alignment and grouping; each width class has its own rule, with
    the functionality unchanged and only how much shows changing; each navigation system's placement is
    stated for each width class.
  Columns: Regions — Id | Region | Role | Landmark; Navigation placement — Navigation system | Width class | Region | Form; Decisions — Decision | State | Decided; Open questions — Question | Owner | Resume condition.
  Cells: Regions › Id — kebab-id; Regions › Landmark — landmark; Navigation placement › Region — region-ref.
  Required: `## Regions`.
  Extra frontmatter: `realizes` is REQUIRED and is exactly `[[product:app-base]]` — one entry, the same
    target `design-system` prescribes (see [[_authoring:wiki-page-types]]). Declaring it is what gives the
    page a build state of its own — see [[_authoring:wiki-fact-placement#realization-membership]] for what
    makes a page an entry and what a code citation naming it grounds.
    `platforms` is REQUIRED — `web` and/or `mobile`, the platforms the pattern applies to; a surface or
    an `information-architecture` page citing the pattern from a platform the list lacks draws a warning.
    `kinds` is REQUIRED — the surface kinds the pattern suits, drawn from the surface kinds
    ([[_authoring:wiki-surface-placement-cell-grammars#surface-placement-cell-grammars]]); a surface
    of a kind the list lacks draws a warning when it cites the pattern.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}}.
-->

## Purpose & usage
<!-- What arrangement this pattern describes and the problem it solves, when a page follows it and —
     just as important — when it does not (the adjacent pattern to reach for instead). One short

## Regions
<!-- One ROW per region of the page: its Id (a kebab id unique on the page, which Navigation

     Every region sits in a landmark. -->

| Id | Region | Role | Landmark |
|---|---|---|---|

## Hierarchy
<!-- What the eye meets first, second and last, and how the arrangement produces that order: order,
     alignment and grouping, not size or color alone. -->

## Responsive arrangement
<!-- One rule per width class (compact, medium, expanded — or the breakpoints the design system's
     layout grid names). The functionality stays the same across width classes; only how much shows
     changes, so a rule says what moves, collapses or reflows, never what disappears from the task. -->

- **<width class>** — <how the regions arrange here>
